intro:
Edinburgh runs the UK's second-largest financial centre, and its project roles have a distinctly regulated flavour: pensions, insurance and asset-management firms delivering compliance-heavy change, alongside two fast-growing fintech unicorn alumni and a public sector serving devolved government. Certified delivery professionals are in structurally short supply in Scotland, which shows in salaries and contract rates. PMP fits the financial programme world; Scrum credentials serve the tech scene spreading through the Exchange district and Leith. Live online training runs continuously through the year for Edinburgh, with weekend Saturday–Sunday and weekday Wednesday–Thursday cohorts timed to sensible local hours; the schedule below shows the exact Edinburgh start and finish for each upcoming batch. Afterwards comes exam application support, mock exams calibrated to the real paper, and continued trainer availability for questions until you clear.

Edinburgh's project economy runs on money and increasingly on code: asset managers and pension giants headquartered here fund continuous regulatory and platform change, while the fintech corridor between the city and Glasgow adds product delivery roles every quarter. Both hiring streams read certification as evidence you can operate inside governed change portfolios. Training runs live online over two days in UK hours, from wherever in the city you are — festival season notwithstanding. Scottish financial-services pay for certified project roles is stronger than many assume; the sourced Edinburgh entries in the table below give the real picture. See the employer list for the asset-management and fintech mix hiring certified talent, and note private cohorts for institutions certifying whole change teams.
